originalTitle: Audrey Werro holds off Britain’s Keely Hodgkinson to win European 800m gold
summary: The Swiss runner set a 1:54.81sec championship best to win European 800m gold, ahead of Keely Hodgkinson in 1:55.01
content: When Audrey Werro was a child, she was so painfully shy that her father told her she had to become a lion every time she raced. In a European women’s 800m final for the ages, she followed that advice to the letter. As the 22-year-old Swiss superstar came around the final bend, she could feel Britain’s Keely Hodgkinson on her shoulder, waiting to strike. The Dutch flyer Femke Broeders-Bol was also close enough to dream too. But Werro was ready to flash her teeth. It didn’t matter that she had been spiked by Broeders-Bol after 200m. Or that she had led the pack into the face of a swirling wind for most of the race. She didn’t succumb. She roared. The noise from the full house of 23,000 home fans was deafening as Hodgkinson tried to pass her on the outside. But the gap never closed. Instead Werro took gold in 1min 54.81sec – a time that broke a championship record that had stood since 1982. It left Hodgkinson looking mightily disappointed after running 1:55.01 to take silver, with Broeders-Bol claiming bronze. But the Olympic champion was also gracious in defeat after. “It doesn’t sting because I was beaten by a great athlete,” said Hodgkinson. “I think I put together a pretty good race. I don’t think I did anything wrong. The thing about the 800m is you have a million different ways of going in your head but I covered every move well. I just didn’t have enough.” There was a moment, though, that she did believe. “In that last 50, I thought I had it,” she said. “But she’s a strong athlete.” As for Werro, her smile told the story given that on Thursday lunchtime it appeared she was out of these Championships after being tripped in the semi-finals. “I am really happy with this medal after a crazy 24 hours,” she said. “When I was a child, my dad used to tell me I had to be a lion. So I decided to do a celebration with that when I crossed the line.” Before the final, Hodgkinson had asked the weather gods for no wind to help her bid for a third successive European title. But they had other ideas. It was whippy and blustery throughout. But that didn’t deter Werro, who went to the front early. And as the bell sounded with the clock showing 56.45, the big three began to stretch away. “Audrey wanted to take it on and, with that wind, I was happy to let her,” said Hodgkinson. “We’re all great athletes and I knew it was going to be close.” It was. And that allowed Hodgkinson to be philosophical after. “We’re all going to win some, lose some,” she said. “Shit happens. Audrey fell over yesterday. She’d made it back. I know what that took out of me a few weeks ago. So yeah, incredible for her. And yeah, life goes on. I’ll go back and train and just hope I get it next time.” That may prove easier said than done given that Werro has run the third, fourth and ninth fastest times in history since June. But only a fool would write the British runner off. There was a second silver medal on the night for Britain in the form of Zharnel Hughes in the men’s 200m. Hughes ran a creditable 20.16, especially given that he has been battling a groin injury. However, he had no answer to the speed of Germany’s Owen Ansah, who powered to victory in 19.95. There was a rare dead heat for bronze between Italy’s Eseosa Fostine Desalu and Switzerland’s Timothé Mumenthaler, who both ran 20.26. However, Ansah’s gold medal was instantly controversial given that last week Germany’s National Anti-Doping Agency had recommended that he should receive a four-year suspension over a possible anti-doping violation. The German authorities claim that is because Ansah missed a test in July. Ansah disputes this. But Hughes will be upgraded to gold if Ansah is banned. Earlier in the night, some of Europe’s biggest stars also shone brightly. First Italy’s Nadia Battocletti added the European 10,000m title to her 5,000m crown with a devastating 28-second burst over the last 200m. Then Norway’s Karsten Warholm ran a championship record time of 46.63 to storm to gold in the men’s 400m hurdles. But perhaps the sweetest moment of the night came when another Italian star, the high jumper Gianmarco Tamberi, asked the crowd to sing happy birthday to his one-year-old daughter, Camilla, after he leaped 2.32m to win gold. They duly obliged too. But there was little joy for Katarina Johnson-Thompson in the women’s heptathlon. The 33-year-old felt the effects of a calf niggle as she finished day one in 16th place with just 3,644 points – a long way behind the leader Adrianna Sulek-Schubert of Poland on 3,968.
chineseTitle: 奥黛丽·韦罗 (Audrey Werro) 力压英国选手基利·霍奇金森 (Keely Hodgkinson) 夺得欧洲 8 亿米金牌
chineseSummary: 这位瑞士选手以1:54.81秒的成绩夺得欧洲800米金牌，领先于基利·霍奇金森(Keely Hodgkinson)的1:55.01
chineseContent: 当奥黛丽·韦罗还是个孩子的时候，她非常害羞，以至于她的父亲告诉她每次比赛时她都必须成为一头狮子。在欧洲女子 800 米决赛中，她完全遵循了这一建议。当这位 22 岁的瑞士超级明星来到最后一个弯道时，她能感觉到英国选手基利·霍奇金森 (Keely Hodgkinson) 站在她的肩膀上，等待出击。荷兰飞行员 Femke Broeders-Bol 也距离梦想很近。但韦罗已经准备好露出牙齿了。尽管她在 200m 后被 Broeders-Bol 秒杀，但这并不重要。或者说，在比赛的大部分时间里，她都带领着狼群面对着旋风。她没有屈服。她咆哮道。当霍奇金森试图从外线超越她时，23,000 名主场球迷的喧闹声震耳欲聋。但差距从未缩小。相反，韦罗以 1 分 54.81 秒的成绩夺得金牌，这一成绩打破了自 1982 年以来一直保持的冠军纪录。这让霍奇金森在以 1 分 55.01 秒的成绩获得银牌后显得非常失望，布罗德斯-波尔获得了铜牌。但这位奥运冠军在失利后也大有风度。 “这并不刺痛，因为我被一位伟大的运动员击败了，”霍奇金森说。 “我认为我组织了一场相当不错的比赛。我不认为我做错了什么。800m 的问题是你脑子里有一百万种不同的方式，但我很好地涵盖了每一个动作。我只是还不够。”不过，有那么一刻，她确实相信了。 “在最后 50 场比赛中，我以为我已经做到了，”她说。 “但她是一名出色的运动员。”至于维罗，她的微笑讲述了这个故事，因为周四午餐时间，她在半决赛中被绊倒后，似乎已经退出了这些锦标赛。 “经过疯狂的 24 小时后，我真的很高兴获得这枚奖牌，”她说。 “当我还是个孩子的时候，我爸爸常常告诉我，我必须成为一名
